procedural_matters: GBR 4034 was represented by Mark Prue.
Jake Brian, crew member of GBR 4034, was present as an observer to the hearing.
The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
AUS 5386 did not come to the hearing, the hearing proceeded in accordance with RRS 63.1(b).
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were 20 knots and very choppy sea.
During the last 30 seconds of the starting procedure, GBR 4034 and AUS 5386 were sailing close-hauled on a collision course, with GBR 4034 on starboard tack and AUS 5386 on port tack.
There was contact between the starboard side of AUS bow and the port side of GBR bow.
The pulpit in GBR 4034 has been pushed into the deck; the first layer of fibreglass has been broken and pushed into the foam core.
GBR 4034 sailed and finished the race.
conclusions: AUS 5386 on port failed to keep clear of GBR 4034 on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.
AUS 5386 did not avoid contact with GBR 4034 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for GBR 4034 the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with AUS 5386 when it became clear that AUS 5386 was not keeping clear. GBR 4034 did not break RRS 14(a).
Since AUS 5386 caused serious damage by her breach, her penalty was to retire as required by RRS 44.1(b).
